title: Tanaris
body: Tanaris is a sea of shifting sand in the far southeast of Kalimdor, south of Thousand Needles and east of Un'Goro Crater. Trolls ruled this land long ago, and the ruins of their old sites still lie half buried among the dunes. Sand trolls of the Sandfury tribe still hold the walled city of Zul'Farrak in the northwest. The goblins of the Steamwheedle Cartel have made the rest of the desert their business. Their town of Gadgetzan lives on water drawn from beneath the dunes, yet the Wastewander nomads have seized most of its wells, and Southsea pirates prey on the cartel's ships from a cove on the eastern coast. Older and stranger powers lie deeper in. Silithid hives drain the desert pools, Dunemaul ogres camp among the troll ruins, and in the south great giants walk before the sealed gates of Uldum. In the eastern mountains the bronze dragonflight keeps the Caverns of Time, where the paths of history meet.

title: Gadgetzan
body: Gadgetzan is the chief town of the Steamwheedle Cartel in Kalimdor, a walled goblin settlement among the dunes of northern Tanaris. Like every cartel town it is neutral ground. Anyone with coin is welcome, and the town's bruisers fall hard on whoever starts trouble, asking only whether the culprit really meant to make them hurt someone. Water is the town's lifeblood and its biggest business, managed by the Gadgetzan Water Company, whose officials fret over every well the nomads steal. Around them work alchemists, smiths, engineers and inventors, and the innkeeper sizes up newcomers for the cage matches fought in the town's arena. Flight masters for both the Alliance and the Horde keep their mounts here.

title: Steamwheedle Port
body: Steamwheedle Port is the cartel's harbor on the northeastern coast of Tanaris, linked by road to Gadgetzan, where ships run to and from Booty Bay. Security Chief Bilgewhizzle keeps the peace on its docks. Stoley tends bar and swears by his Steamwheedle bilge rum, thick as gravel and fiery as lava. A haughty fashion designer procures the latest styles for queens and warchiefs, a troll mystic named Yeh'kinya pursues his studies along the shore, and the gnome soothsayer Narain Soothfancy keeps house just to the north. South of the port waits Torta, a turtle whose husband Tooga went out to fetch dinner and has not found his way home.

title: Noonshade Ruins
body: On the road between Gadgetzan and Steamwheedle Port lie the Noonshade Ruins, a scatter of ancient troll stonework half buried in the sand. Whoever raised them is long gone. The ruins now shelter Wastewander thieves and bandits, who lie in wait among the stones, and starving blisterpaw hyenas and scorpid hunters prowl the dunes around them. Purple lotus grows among the broken walls for those bold enough to pick it.

title: Waterspring Field
body: Waterspring Field, east of Gadgetzan, is the reason the town can survive at all. The goblins raised water towers here to pump the hidden reserves beneath the desert. The Wastewander nomads took the field for themselves, and their rogues, shadow mages and assassins now guard the towers and the wells the Gadgetzan Water Company counts as its own. Their leader, Caliph Scorpidsting, is found here among them, and the Water Company has posted a price on his head for murdering its workers and seizing its property.

title: Lost Rigger Cove
body: Ringed by mountains south of Steamwheedle Port lies Lost Rigger Cove, the hideout of the Southsea pirates. Their walled town has docks and a shipyard, and cargo taken from cartel ships lies about it, including the rum shipment Captain Cuergo stole from Stoley. The cartel pays the pirates protection money, yet lately they ignore the bargain. The pirate Andre Firebeard is wanted for crimes against Steamwheedle and Gadgetzan, and a goblin cutthroat named Kregg Keelhaul is sometimes seen in the cove. A treasure map even claims Cuergo buried a chest of gold on a beach further south.

title: Southbreak Shore
body: South of Lost Rigger Cove the coast opens into Southbreak Shore, a long flat beach washed by the South Seas. Surf gliders, great sea turtles, haul themselves through the shallows, and the beach belongs to giants: coast striders wade along the tide line and a deep dweller lurks in the water beyond. Few travelers linger. On a small island just offshore lives a gnome named Winkey, keeping his own company.

title: Caverns of Time
body: In the mountains of eastern Tanaris a great cavern opens into the realm of Nozdormu, the Timeless One. Here the bronze dragonflight has watched over the flow of time since the world was young, and its guardians bar any who would meddle with it. Before the entrance stands Anachronos, heir of Nozdormu, in his true dragon form, and nearby wait his far less welcoming dragonkin companions Tick, Chronalis and Occulus, who suffer no mortal to come near.

parts.body: In these days the bronze flight receives mortal visitors. At the threshold the Steward of Time greets travelers as if he had expected them, warns of the dangers that lie beyond his hall, and sends them down to the Keepers of Time in the depths. Below, tunnels called timeways lead into moments of history that strange beings are trying to unmake.

title: Broken Pillar
body: South of Gadgetzan a few toppled columns mark the Broken Pillar, the remains of a troll site lost to the sands. Its newest resident is Marvon Rivetseeker, a goblin scholar from Ratchet who crashed his zeppelin nearby and decided to begin his research where he landed. From his camp he studies the troll ruins of the desert and the ornaments of Gahz'ridian the old trolls carved in honor of the hydra Gahz'rilla, and he speaks of what he once saw within the Sunken Temple.

title: Abyssal Sands
body: The Abyssal Sands are the empty heart of Tanaris, a rolling waste of dunes between Gadgetzan and the southern ruins. Little shade and less water can be found here. Fire rocs and their larger kin circle overhead, glasshide basilisks bask on the dunes, and packs of blisterpaw hyenas and scorpids roam the sand in search of prey. Whirling vortexes of wind drift across the waste, and travelers speak of a great firebird that is sometimes seen soaring above it.

title: Sandsorrow Watch
body: West of Gadgetzan, Sandfury trolls guard Sandsorrow Watch, an outpost of watch towers standing over a pool of open water, a rare treasure in the desert. Firecallers, hideskinners and axe throwers patrol its sands, and they do not welcome goblin surveyors. The Gadgetzan Water Company covets the pool all the same and sends its junior surveyors to sample it in plain sight of the trolls. A troll called Jin'Zallah the Sandbringer is said to walk among them.

A junior surveyor who came to sample it was set upon at the water's edge by something that crawled, and the attack forced the Water Company to admit that the stories of strange bugs drinking the desert dry were no nomad trick. For Gadgetzan it was the first warning of the silithid.

title: Zul'Farrak
body: In the northwest of Tanaris rise the walls of Zul'Farrak, city of the Sandfury trolls, ruthless sand trolls steeped in dark magic who attack anyone who approaches. Warleader Krazzilak prowls before its gates. Legends cling to the place. A hydra god, Gahz'rilla, is said to dwell in a sacred pool within its walls, and the persecutors of the martyr Theka are said to scuttle about his shrine, cursed into scarabs. Many are drawn inside all the same: Sergeant Bly led his band in hunting treasure, the Prophecy of Mosh'aru lies on tablets within, and the smith Trenton Lighthammer of Gadgetzan still remembers with dread the warband that once marched out of it to lay waste to the land.

title: The Noxious Lair
body: On the western edge of Tanaris, above the jungles of Un'Goro Crater, the ground sinks into a broad hollow where pools of water once gathered. They are gone now, drained by the Centipaar silithid who have dug their hive into the sand. Their workers, tunnelers and stingers swarm over the hollow, their eggs lie clustered in the earth, and their sandreavers guard the hive mounds. The Gadgetzan Water Company wants to know what these bugs are, and seeks parts of them for Alchemist Pestlezugg to study. A great devourer named Soriid is said to hunt among the hives.

title: Dunemaul Compound
body: Not long ago a large band of nomadic Dunemaul ogres wandered into Tanaris and claimed a stretch of desert south of Gadgetzan, building a compound there. Brutes and enforcers guard it, warlocks and ogre mages practice their crude magic, and smaller bands have spread out to occupy the old troll ruins nearby. In Gadgetzan, Andi Lynn fears the force the ogres could build and wants the compound broken before it grows, beginning with its leader, Gor'marok the Ravager. Two rarely seen ogres, Cyclok the Mad and Omgorn the Lost, prowl the camp as well.

title: Eastmoon Ruins
body: West of the Gaping Chasm lie the Eastmoon Ruins, ancient troll stonework slowly swallowed by the dunes. The Dunemaul ogres have spread here from their compound, and their warlocks and ogre mages have made the ruins a camp of their own. Glasshide basilisks and blisterpaw hyenas haunt the edges, purple lotus grows in the shelter of the old walls, and the rarely seen ogre wanderer Omgorn the Lost passes through.

title: Southmoon Ruins
body: North of the Valley of the Watchers stand the Southmoon Ruins, another troll site from the days when trolls held this land. Dunemaul ogres camp among the fallen stones. The ground here is rich in Gahz'ridian, the strange element the old trolls carved into ornaments in honor of their hydra god, and a goblin treasure hunter at the Broken Pillar rewards those who bring him pieces. Searing rocs circle overhead.

title: The Gaping Chasm
body: Southeast of Gadgetzan the desert splits open into the Gaping Chasm, now a hive of the Hazzali silithid. Wasps, swarmers and stingers boil out of its great mounds, while workers and tunnelers dig ever deeper below. Junior Surveyor Scrimshank of the Gadgetzan Water Company was sent here, and his last report spoke of the same strange bugs before he went missing. A ravenous silithid called Haarka is feared in the depths, and near the chasm lies a crashed gnomish homing robot, OOX-17/TN, waiting for someone to come to its rescue.

title: Thistleshrub Valley
body: In the southwestern corner of Tanaris lies Thistleshrub Valley, a low basin where great cacti grow thick in the heat. Its guardians are living plants: gnarled thistleshrubs and rootshapers that lash out at anything that comes near, and dew collectors that store precious water in special glands. That water has drawn more than one schemer from Gadgetzan. Marin Noggenfogger sought the glands for a drink to quench his thirst, and Tran'rek of Gadgetzan wants a closer look at the valley's cactus, if only someone else will clear the way first.

title: Valley of the Watchers
body: In the far southwest of Tanaris a valley runs between the mountains to a great sealed gate, the entrance to Uldum. Few believe the place behind it is more than a myth. The gate cannot be forced, and huge giants, the Dune Smashers, walk the valley floor as if keeping watch over it. Before the gate stands a stone pedestal, silent to those who pass it by. Prospector Gunstan of the Explorers' League keeps a lonely camp in the valley, among the few who come here at all.

title: Land's End Beach
body: Land's End Beach is the southernmost shore of Tanaris, in the far southeast of Kalimdor, where the desert finally runs out into the South Seas. Surf gliders by the dozen crawl through the breakers. A mermaid named Meridith dwells in the waters here, and she still treasures the day she pulled a gnome from the wreck of his flying machine on this very beach. That gnome was Narain Soothfancy, who had hidden a precious book on a small island further south and crashed on the way home. A pirate's treasure map claims that Captain Cuergo buried his gold on this shore, by a mast, a flag and bones.

title: Senior Surveyor Fizzledowser
body: Senior Surveyor Fizzledowser of the Gadgetzan Water Company has one great worry: with the nomads holding the wells, the town must find its water somewhere else. His answer is to survey the desert for fresh sources, and he will sign on almost any likely stranger as a temporary junior-grade surveyor, hand over a dowsing widget and send them off to sample far-flung pools, even those within sight of the Sandfury trolls. He leans on his top assistant, Junior Surveyor Scrimshank, and counts the alchemist Pestlezugg an old friend.

parts.body: Fizzledowser owns that he should have warned his recruits. Reports of strange bugs drinking up the desert's water had been coming in for some time, and he had waved them off as one more nomad trick, until his own surveyor was ambushed at Sandsorrow Watch. Now at least, he says, the company knows.

Then he lost Scrimshank. His top assistant never returned from the Gaping Chasm, and Fizzledowser, mourning a good goblin, pinned his hopes on whatever the recovered survey gear had recorded. The company's research, he now believes, points to the bugs being steered by a third party, which bodes ill for the whole desert.

Fizzledowser is not thrilled about handing out the company's valuable information for nothing, but he has known Pestlezugg for years. When the alchemist urged that everyone be warned of the bugs, he copied the report for all to read.

title: Chief Engineer Bilgewhizzle
body: Chief Engineer Bilgewhizzle of the Gadgetzan Water Company is as fierce about profit as he is about justice for the Wastewander nomads who stole his wells. He rewards those who thin the nomads' ranks, pays the company's bounty on their leader Caliph Scorpidsting, and sells off the model 4711-FTZ power sources that once ran the wells, now in surplus thanks to the thieves, reminding buyers that nothing is free in Gadgetzan. He dreams aloud of importing water from the icy springs of Dun Morogh. He also wants back his cherished divino-matic rod, the tool he uses to find new water holes, stolen by a mercenary named Sergeant Bly who led his band into Zul'Farrak.
sources: quest 243 reward text (4711-FTZ power sources, over abundance because of the nomads, nothing's free in Gadgetzan)
quest 654 completion text (import water from the icy springs of Dun Morogh)
quest 2768 description (divino-matic rod, Sergeant Bly, Zul'Farrak)
notes: Unchanged in conversion: nothing to hide. Earlier: Fact-check: verified. Quest 243 chain (Zinge, Horde) is Undercity's and not used. 'Dreams aloud' paraphrases 654: until we can afford to import water. Faction 0: template 475.

title: Marin Noggenfogger
body: Marin Noggenfogger is a Gadgetzan goblin with a terrible thirst and a nose for profit. Living out in the desert is rough, he complains, and standing about in the heat leaves him parched. Lately he has set his hopes on the dew collectors of Thistleshrub Valley, living plants said to hoard water in glands of their own. A drink brewed from one of those, he reckons, would put an end to his thirst for good.
sources: npc_text 1493 (so thirsty standing outside in this heat)
quests 2605, 2606 (Sprinkle an excellent chef; a little eccentric)
quests 2641, 2661, 2662 (Violet Powder; millions; such a kidder)
notes: Check: opening and parts reworded so they do not repeat 44032 word for word (2605, 2606, 2662); content unchanged. Converted: The chain's course moved out of the opening: the dreadful taste and Sprinkle to part 1 (QUEST_DONE 2606), the elixir and the favor to part 2 (QUEST_DONE 2662). The opening keeps his thirst and his idea (npc_text 1493, quest 2605 description). Earlier: Fact-check: 'sell by the millions' made 'make millions on' (2662). Not called baron (Cataclysm). Faction 0: 474. Rest verified.

parts.body: One taste of the gland's water was enough to make Marin gag, yet he refused to give up. He passed the dew to Sprinkle, his friend and a fine cook, who calls him a good guy if a little eccentric and sighed that of course he needed her help yet again.

Her secret mushroom powder transformed the brew. The result was the Noggenfogger Elixir, which Marin now sells and expects to make millions on. Sprinkle insists that he owes her one for it. Marin laughs that off as one of her jokes.

title: Curgle Cranklehop
body: Curgle Cranklehop is a Gadgetzan inventor with a soft spot for birds. He is helping the druids save the hippogryphs of Feralas, whose numbers are dwindling under the blight of the Gordunni ogres, and to that end he built the Super Egg-O-Matic, a machine that weighs, measures and packs any hippogryph egg brought to it. He collects eggs of every quality, grieving gently over the ones that cannot be saved, and sends crates of them to Erelas Ambersky in Rut'theran Village to hatch. His latest invention, the Super Snapper FX, takes pictures of anything it is aimed at.
sources: npc_text 1519 (Super Egg-O-Matic, aiding the druids to save the hippogryphs, Gordunni)
quests 2741 reward text (weighed, measured and packaged), 2747, 2750
quest 3022 (crate to Erelas Ambersky in Rut'theran)
feralas.json 35735 (the Stave of Equinex chain uses the camera; not retold)
notes: Unchanged in conversion: nothing to hide. Earlier: Fact-check: 'ships the best' made 'sends crates of them' (3022 crate of eggs; 2748). 'Soft spot for birds' kept as a gloss. Egg quests not triggers. Faction 0: 35. Rest verified.

title: Marvon Rivetseeker
body: Marvon Rivetseeker is a goblin scientist from Ratchet and a treasure hunter at heart. He came to Tanaris by zeppelin to study its troll ruins, crashed, and simply began his research where he landed, at the Broken Pillar. He collects the Gahz'ridian ornaments the old trolls carved after the hydra Gahz'rilla, finding them with a detector helmet of his own invention. He once entered the Sunken Temple and barely escaped through its ooze-flooded halls, and all he remembers of it is a large circular room filled with serpent statues. He has sent for a round stone bearing the same serpent symbol, hoping it will tell him more.
sources: quests 3380, 3445 (left his home in Ratchet to study the troll ruins in Tanaris)
quests 3446, 3447 (circle of statues holds the secret to a greater treasure)
notes: Converted: His returning memories (the trap, the altar, the treasure) moved to part 1 on QUEST_DONE 3444, where the stone brings them back; the opening keeps what he says before it (3444 description). Earlier: Fact-check: 'years ago' made 'once' (3444); the treasure belief moved from the altar to the circle of statues (3447). Sunken Temple quests not triggers. Faction 0: 474. Rest verified.

parts.body: With the stone in hand, his memories came back. The room had six balconies, each with a serpent statue at its edge. Pushing one sprang a trap that nearly killed him, and from the ledge he glimpsed an altar to Hakkar below. He believes the circle of statues holds the secret to an even greater treasure.

title: Yeh'kinya
body: Yeh'kinya is an old troll mystic living at Steamwheedle Port. Time and drink, he admits, have dulled his outer senses, though his inner eyes remain strong. His studies turn on an ancient god whom he will not yet name, and he believes the screechers of the Feralas vales are kin to that god, their spirits bound to him still. He wants someone to go and gather their essence, and to whoever does, he promises to reveal more about the god.
sources: npc_text 2140 (time and drink have dulled my outer senses)
quest 8181 reward text and creature_text 8579 (Blood and souls for Hakkar)
warcraft.wiki.gg/wiki/Yeh'kinya (troll at Steamwheedle Port, worships Hakkar)
notes: Check: opening and parts reworded so they do not repeat 44034 and 44035 word for word on the same triggers (3520, 3528, 8181). Part 3's cry to Hakkar dropped: creature_text 8579 group 1 is not spoken by any script in this database; replaced by the 8181 reward text (that meddling prospector). Converted: The prophecy he tells moved to part 1 (QUEST_DONE 3520), the egg he took to part 2 (QUEST_DONE 3528), his allegiance to Hakkar to part 3 (QUEST_DONE 8181, the turn-in to Yeh'kinya himself; 8181 starts from Ironboot, whom mod-individual-progression shows from state 3, so it cannot fire earlier). The opening keeps his greeting and his first request (npc_text 2140, quest 3520 description). Hakkar's return at Zul'Gurub stays open setting in Stranglethorn; only Yeh'kinya's part in it is told here. Earlier: Fact-check: verified. Yeh'kinya's later gossip (2139, re-summoning the avatar) not used. Faction 0: 474.

parts.body: Once the essence was in his hands, Yeh'kinya named the god: Hakkar the Soulflayer, whose return the trolls foretell, some as a coming glory for their race, others as the end of all things. The myth itself he professes to doubt. What he wants, he says, is to keep the power in Hakkar's essence out of the hands of any who would misuse it.

His tale sent helpers across the world, to Zul'Farrak for the tablets of Mosh'aru, to Jintha'Alor for an ancient egg and into the Sunken Temple for the essence of Hakkar's avatar. When the filled egg came back to him and stirred, Yeh'kinya mused that the myths might be true after all, and he kept it, vowing that no evil hand would ever touch it.

The truth was darker. Yeh'kinya had served Hakkar all along. When his helpers came back to demand the egg, he cursed the meddling prospector Ironboot and declared it too late to save the world: the Soulflayer was already reborn in Zul'Gurub and growing in power, and with mock gratitude he told them their help had sped his return.

title: Prospector Ironboot
body: Prospector Ironboot is an old dwarf scholar who works among the goblins of Steamwheedle Port, far from the halls of his own people. He has studied the troll legends of Hakkar the Soulflayer for a long time, above all the prophecy of Mosh'aru, which the trolls set down upon tablets, and he fears that what those tablets hold will prove a great threat to the world.
sources: quest 8181 reward text (that old dwarf Ironboot, meddling prospector)
notes: Check: parts reworded so they do not repeat 44035 word for word on the same triggers (5065, 8181, 8182); content unchanged. Converted: The six tablets moved to part 1 (QUEST_ACCEPT 5065), the egg's true purpose to part 2 (QUEST_ACCEPT 8181), the Zandalari to part 3 (QUEST_ACCEPT 8182, his own quest; it ends with Molthor in Stranglethorn). The opening keeps his scholarship and his fear (5065 completion text). mod-individual-progression shows Ironboot from state 3 (npc_ipp_zg), so every trigger is reachable only then; no tag needed. Earlier: Fact-check: verified. 'Scholar' from 5065 (I have studied long). Faction 0: 474. Molthor and Yojamba Isle belong to Stranglethorn (3312) and are only mentioned.

parts.body: Ironboot's studies had shown him what the troll left out. The prophecy Yeh'kinya relied on rested on two tablets of Mosh'aru, but the dwarf knows of six, and he dreads what the missing four will say. Two of them, he has learned, lie with the Mossflayer trolls in the Eastern Plaguelands.

His delvings into the tablets bore grim news. The egg was a cradle, not a prison: through it Hakkar himself could be born again. Ironboot sent the troll's helpers back to Yeh'kinya to demand it, praying it was not too late.

It was too late. Ironboot now puts his faith in the Zandalari, whose envoys have camped on Yojamba Isle near Stranglethorn, and sends heroes to their leader Molthor, hoping these trolls know a way to stop Hakkar before his new reign can spread across Azeroth.

title: Narain Soothfancy
body: Narain Soothfancy is a gnome who lives just north of Steamwheedle Port and calls himself a psychic, though his guesses rarely land: he will press an unopened envelope to his forehead and announce what lies inside, usually wrongly. A copy of Soothsaying for Dummies sits by his door. He claims a crash on Land's End Beach gave him his super-gnomish powers, and he nurses a long list of grudges, chief among them his arch-enemy, Doctor Weavil.
sources: npc_text 7902 (envelope guess; Soothsaying for Dummies book)
quest 8597 (crash gave him super-gnomish psychic powers)
warcraft.wiki.gg/wiki/Narain_Soothfancy (lived north of Steamwheedle Port; Azuregos: terrible psychic, amazing engineer)
gameobject 177226 Book Soothsaying for Dummies in area 977
npc_text 7897 (Azuregos: terrible, terrible psychic but an amazing engineer)
notes: Check: Weavil in the opening kept: dustwallow.json 1505 names him Narain's sworn enemy openly, Narain's gossip (npc_text 7902) does not name him, and the opening does not say Weavil took the book. Small wording changes in parts 2 and 3. Converted: Azuregos's judgment moved to part 1 (QUEST_DONE 8576, when the ledger reaches him), Stewvul to part 2 (QUEST_ACCEPT 8577), Weavil's destruction of the book to part 3 (QUEST_ACCEPT 8620), the mermaid to part 4 (QUEST_DONE 8599). The opening keeps his gossip (npc_text 7902) and names Weavil as his enemy, which dustwallow.json 1505 already tells openly. All triggers follow 8576 (an Ahn'Qiraj chain), so no era tag. Earlier: Fact-check: 'prefers not to discuss it' made 'insists it could never work' (8599 reward). Azuregos quote confirmed by npc_text 7897. Faction 0: 35. Rest verified.

parts.body: Behind the bluster he is a gifted engineer. When the blue dragon Azuregos needed an arcanite buoy built, he sent his plans to Narain, calling him a terrible, terrible psychic but an amazing engineer. Narain grumbled that the old goat knows he cannot read a word of Draconic.

Another grudge is older. His ex-best friend forever, Stewvul, stole his scrying goggles long ago, broke his heart in five places and left him here to rot, or so Narain tells it, and his crystal ball places the thief either at the Greymane Wall of Silverpine or somewhere far stranger.

Doctor Weavil has struck at him through his most precious book. The only known copy of volume two of Draconic for Dummies, which Narain had hidden on an island far to the south, was booknapped, then torn into eight pieces and scattered to the wind, and Narain lays the blame squarely at his arch-enemy's feet.

A mermaid loves him. Meridith of Land's End Beach, who pulled him from the wreck of his flying machine, has sent word of her feelings. Narain fidgets at the very idea. She is a fish, he protests, and he is a gnome. It could never work out.

title: Anachronos
body: Anachronos, heir of Nozdormu the Timeless One, keeps watch before the Caverns of Time in his true dragon form, a great bronze dragon watching over the approach to his master's realm, his dragonkin companions never far away. He has few words for the mortals who pass, and those few are grim. He speaks as though a war were close at hand: this time, he insists, the first strike must be theirs, so that the mistakes of the past are not repeated. To passing visitors he does not say what those mistakes were.
sources: warcraft.wiki.gg/wiki/Anachronos (heir of Nozdormu; qiraji attacked the Caverns; sealed with Fandral; made the scepter; Fandral shattered it after Valstann's death; shards to Vaelastrasz, Azuregos, Eranikus)
quest 8519 reward text (gathered the shards, charge of the Dragonflights)
quest 8555 reward text (distrust towards your kind)
npc_text 7742 (we must make the first strike; mistakes of the past)
notes: Check: the War of the Shifting Sands history (Anachronos calling the dragonflights and sealing the wall with Fandral) dropped from the opening: his part in it is shown in the crystal vision of 8519 and told in its reward text, both in the Silithus-owned Scepter chain, and Fandral's role is held back in darnassus.json. The opening now holds only what a Tanaris visitor meets: his form, his post and his gossip (npc_text 7742). Silithus's conversion must tell the forging, the shattering and his distrust (8519, 8555 reward texts), since silithus.json 137728 left them to this entry. Converted: Cross-zone spoilers removed: the forging of the Scepter of the Shifting Sands, Fandral shattering it, the shards given to guardian dragons, and his distrust of mortals (quests 8519, 8555 reward texts) are revelations of the Scepter chain, which Silithus owns (silithus.json 137728; 8286 on, 8729, 8742). No Tanaris trigger can reveal them, so they are dropped here, not moved. mod-individual-progression rewrites 8555 in every state (aq_gate_quest.sql), another reason to leave it to Silithus. Anachronos is not phased by the module, so no era tag; his gossip (npc_text 7742) reread: classic. Earlier: Fact-check: verified. The Scepter chain (8286 on, 8555, 8742, 8743) runs from Silithus to Silithus and is left to Silithus; only TALK is used. True dragon form: display 2719 with combat reach 10 (dragon model) in 3.3.5; the elf form is Cataclysm. Faction 0: 776 (Brood of Nozdormu, neutral).

title: Andormu
body: Andormu is a bronze dragon of the Keepers of Time who wears the shape of an elf, at times a grown man and at times a child, both sometimes seen at once. With his sister Nozari he leads the keepers in the Caverns of Time while Nozdormu is away. Small meddlers hardly concern him, such as a greedy wizard nudging the past to better his station. What troubles him now is worse: strange beings seen more and more often across the timeways, trying to alter the course of history itself. The keepers dare not risk themselves, so Andormu welcomes heroes from Azeroth to defend the timeways in their place.
sources: warcraft.wiki.gg/wiki/Andormu (bronze dragon, elf visage, adult and child forms at the same time, sister Nozari, co-leader of the Keepers of Time)
creature_text 19932 and 19933 (Andormu and Nozari: greedy wizard, beings tampering with the timeways, master away, heroes due to arrive)
creature_text 19932 groups 1 and 2 (greedy wizard improving his station)
notes: Unchanged in conversion: nothing to hide; no era tag, since mod-individual-progression shows Andormu (20130, npc_ipp_tbc) only from state 8, so his only trigger cannot fire earlier. Dialogue reread (creature_text 19932, 19933): Burning Crusade text, nothing from Cataclysm. Earlier: Fact-check: 'no patience for small meddlers' reworded to his line (19932: not talking about a greedy wizard improving his station). Instance chains not used. Faction 0: 1779. Rest verified.

title: Bugs in the Water
body: With the Wastewander nomads holding its wells, the Gadgetzan Water Company has gone looking for new water. There is water to be had in the desert, Senior Surveyor Fizzledowser insists, for those smart enough to survey it first, and he has taken on temporary junior surveyors to find it. The first assignment is a pool beside Sandsorrow Watch, in plain sight of the Sandfury trolls: tap a sample with a dowsing widget and bring it back. It sounds simple enough, and the company badly needs it to be, for without the wells the town's water supply will soon run dry.
sources: quests 32 and 162 reward texts (silithid named by Zilzibin Drumlore and Gracina Spiritmight)
notes: Check: small wording changes in parts 1 and 2 to avoid repeats with 44012 and 44016. Converted: Every step of the chain moved out of the opening into parts on the turn-ins where it is revealed: the ambush (992), the first analysis and Scrimshank's disappearance (82), his fate (10), the malign force (110), the copied report (113). The scholars' naming of the silithid (32, 162 reward texts) dropped: those turn-ins end in Orgrimmar and Darnassus, and darnassus.json 165710 part 1 tells it on DONE 162. Earlier: Fact-check: verified. Darnassus (165710) owns Gracina and 4508; the follow-up March of the Silithid (4493/4494 from the capitals) and Pestlezugg's Un'Goro hunt (4496, 4507) are left to those zones and Un'Goro. 32 and 162 are not used as triggers (they end in Orgrimmar and Darnassus).

parts.body: The surveyor came back with tales of an ambush by some crawling horror. Fizzledowser confessed he had heard reports of bug-creatures sucking up the desert's water and dismissed them as nomad shenanigans. Now he wanted to know the enemy, and sent for parts from the Centipaar of the Noxious Lair, where water pools once lay, for the alchemist Pestlezugg to examine.

Pestlezugg found the parts unlike any insect he had ever seen, almost as if the bugs were controlled by an outside force. And there was an emergency. Fizzledowser's top assistant, Scrimshank, had gone missing in the Gaping Chasm southeast of town, and the last word from him told of more of the same bugs.

Only Scrimshank's surveying gear came back from the chasm. Fizzledowser mourned a good goblin and hoped his death had not been in vain, for the research so far suggested that the bugs, too cunning for their own good, might be under the influence of a third party.

Pestlezugg's analysis confirmed it. The bugs are controlled by a powerful and malignant force and have been changed into pure ravagers. The alchemist warned that they threaten not only Gadgetzan but all of southern Kalimdor, perhaps the whole of Azeroth, and urged that everyone be told.

Fizzledowser, never thrilled to give company information away, made copies at his old friend's urging, and the report went out to scholars in Orgrimmar and Darnassus who have studied the creatures of Azeroth, in the hope that they could say what the threat is and how it might be stopped.

title: Wastewander Justice
body: The Wastewander nomads have seized almost every well in Tanaris, and without them Gadgetzan's water will soon run dry. Chief Engineer Bilgewhizzle of the Gadgetzan Water Company calls it a matter of justice, goblin style, and his first order is to thin the nomads' ranks, starting with the bandits and thieves east of town. Meanwhile Spigot Operator Luglunket pays a company care package for every handful of water pouches taken from the nomads, since that water was the company's to begin with. Wanted posters in Gadgetzan and Steamwheedle Port name the nomads' leader, Caliph Scorpidsting, for murdering company workers and stealing its resources and property.
sources: gameobject_queststarter 142122, 150075 (Wanted Posters in areas 977 and 976) for 2781
notes: Converted: The campaign's progress moved out of the opening: the second wave of targets to part 1 (QUEST_DONE 1690), the turning of the tide to part 2 (QUEST_DONE 1691), the caliph's death to part 3 (QUEST_DONE 2781). The opening keeps the situation and the first order. Earlier: Fact-check: verified. Faction 0: all AllowableRaces 0. 2781 starts from the wanted posters.

parts.body: The bandits and thieves fell in enough numbers that the company could begin to plan how to win back its wells, but Bilgewhizzle was far from done. Next came the stronger ranks east and southeast of town, the rogues, assassins and shadow mages who guard the stolen wells, a nasty lot by his own account.

With those ranks thinned as well, the nomads were few enough that the Gadgetzan Water Company could finally take the fight to them, and Bilgewhizzle began to speak of taking back what was rightfully the company's.

Caliph Scorpidsting's head was brought to Bilgewhizzle, who declared that justice was served and paid the bounty in the company's name. With the caliph dead, he hopes, the squatters may at last be pushed off Gadgetzan's wells.

title: The Noggenfogger Elixir
body: Marin Noggenfogger of Gadgetzan is thirsty, as anyone who stands about in the Tanaris heat must be. He has heard of strange creatures to the southwest, the dew collectors of Thistleshrub Valley, which store water in special glands, and he is sure that a drink made from one would quench his thirst. All he needs is someone willing to go out to the cactus garden where the dew collectors live and bring a laden gland back to him, so that he can taste it for himself.
notes: Converted: The chain's course moved out of the opening: the taste and Sprinkle to part 1 (QUEST_DONE 2605), the Violet Tragan to part 2 (QUEST_ACCEPT 2641), the elixir to part 3 (QUEST_DONE 2662). The opening keeps Marin's idea (2605 description). Earlier: Fact-check: verified. Faction 0: AllowableRaces 0. The Hinterlands file does not use 2641.

parts.body: The gland's water tasted dreadful. Rather than give up, Marin had a brilliant idea: send the dew to his friend Sprinkle, an excellent cook, and have her make it go down easier. If it was going to taste that bad, he reasoned, it should at least have some kick.

Sprinkle knew just the thing. As a child she had survived her sister's horrible cooking with a secret ingredient, a mushroom called the Violet Tragan, which grows only underwater in a small lake of the Hinterlands. Add it to anything, she promised, and it tastes great.

Ground into a violet powder and mixed with the dew, the mushroom produced the Noggenfogger Elixir. Marin, delighted, now plans to make millions on it and shoos his helpers aside so they do not block his business. Sprinkle reminds him he owes her a favor. Marin calls her such a kidder.

title: The Southsea Shakedown
body: The Steamwheedle Cartel pays the Southsea pirates of Lost Rigger Cove to leave its ships alone, but lately the pirates have taken the money and kept raiding. The cartel has leaned on Security Chief Bilgewhizzle of Steamwheedle Port to teach them a lesson, and since he cannot leave the docks he deputizes whoever will go. A wanted decree authorizes lethal force against the pirate Andre Firebeard, adding that his head may stand in for him at his hearing. The port has its own grievances. Captain Cuergo stole Stoley's last shipment of rum just when Stoley needed it to settle a bet with Sea Wolf MacKinley of Booty Bay, and the Haughty Modiste wants Southsea hats by the score for the elite of Azerothian society.
sources: quest 2875 description (lethal force, head as proxy)
notes: Converted: Opening was over the Story range (153 words) and held outcomes: Andre's death moved to part 1 (QUEST_DONE 2875), the ship schedules found on a pirate to part 2 (QUEST_DONE 2876, item-started, turned in to Bilgewhizzle), the hats' fate to part 3 (QUEST_DONE 8365). The opening keeps the situation (8366, 2875, 2873, 8365 descriptions). Earlier: Fact-check: verified. 2872 (start, Booty Bay) and 2874 (turn-in, Booty Bay) not used: Stranglethorn may use them. 2876 starts from a dropped item; it is described but not a trigger. Faction 0: all AllowableRaces 0.

parts.body: Andre Firebeard's head reached Bilgewhizzle at last. So the pirate would make his trial after all, the security chief remarked, and he paid for services rendered, assuring the one who brought it that the small print on the contract was quite harmless.

One of the pirates was carrying the schedules of shipments between the port and Booty Bay, past and future, with ships marked for great loot or a hard fight. Bilgewhizzle was disturbed: with such a list, he said, a pirate captain could have himself a field day.

The hats went to the Haughty Modiste, who means to have them cleaned and personalized and expects them to make her quite a bit of money, though she suggested that whoever fetched them spend some of the reward on a bath.

title: The Egg of Hakkar
body: The troll mystic Yeh'kinya of Steamwheedle Port seeks the spirits of the vale screechers of Feralas, cousins, he says, of an old, old god whose spirits are still linked to him. He hands out a bramble wand for the task: strike down a screecher, wave the bramble over its body to coax its spirit out, and touch the spirit to gather its essence. Bring back the bramble and the essence, Yeh'kinya promises, and he will tell more of the old god of which he spoke.
notes: Converted: The chain moved out of the opening into parts: the prophecy and the tablets (QUEST_DONE 3520), the egg (QUEST_ACCEPT 4787, Yeh'kinya's own quest though filed under the Hinterlands; 3527 is a Zul'Farrak quest left for an instance file), the avatar's essence (QUEST_DONE 3528, given and turned in at Yeh'kinya; swamp_of_sorrows.json does not use it). Earlier: Fact-check: verified. Chain starts and ends with Yeh'kinya in Tanaris. 4787 (Hinterlands sort) and 3528 (Sunken Temple sort) are not used by hinterlands.json or swamp_of_sorrows.json. Only 3520 is a trigger. Faction 0.

parts.body: The old god is Hakkar the Soulflayer, and the trolls have a prophecy that he will one day return. Yeh'kinya claimed not to believe it, only to want the god's power kept from those who would abuse it. The prophecy of Mosh'aru, he said, told how to contain Hakkar's essence. Its two tablets lay in Zul'Farrak, one with the long-dead martyr Theka, one with the hydromancer Velratha.

Fused together, the tablets spoke of an ancient egg, a relic of the days when trolls ruled vast empires, with the power to hold the essence of Hakkar. It lay hidden in a cave behind the amphitheater atop Jintha'Alor in the Hinterlands, and Yeh'kinya wanted it brought to him.

Carried into the Sanctum of the Fallen God within the Sunken Temple, the egg stirred the dead god. His avatar came forth and was slain, and its essence was drawn into the egg. When the filled egg stirred with life, Yeh'kinya wondered whether the myths were true, and took it into his keeping, promising to keep it from evil hands.

title: The Lost Tablets of Mosh'aru
body: After the egg of Hakkar passed into Yeh'kinya's hands, the dwarf Prospector Ironboot of Steamwheedle Port came forward with a warning: the troll had not told the truth. The two tablets brought to him spoke of containing Hakkar's essence, but there was more to the legend. Ironboot had found that there are six tablets of Mosh'aru, not two, and he feared what the others would reveal. The third and fourth, he said, are held by the Mossflayer trolls of the Eastern Plaguelands.
notes: Converted: The chain moved out of the opening into parts: the last tablets (QUEST_DONE 5065), the egg's true purpose (QUEST_ACCEPT 8181), Yeh'kinya's gloating (QUEST_DONE 8181), the Zandalari (QUEST_ACCEPT 8182; it ends with Molthor, stranglethorn.json 3312 uses no quest). The opening keeps Ironboot's warning (5065 description). Ironboot appears from state 3 under mod-individual-progression, so every trigger is reachable only then. Earlier: Fact-check: verified. Starts and ends with Ironboot in Tanaris (8182 ends with Molthor; stranglethorn 3312 Yojamba Isle is a place and uses no quest). 5065 requires 3528. Faction 0.

parts.body: The fifth and sixth tablets were held by the Smolderthorn trolls within Blackrock Spire, a dark mountain of fire between the Burning Steppes and the Searing Gorge, and Ironboot sent his helpers there while he pored over the third and fourth.

Reading the tablets together, Ironboot found the hidden half of the legend. The egg was never meant to contain the Soulflayer. Hakkar's true form could be born again through the very egg into which his essence had been captured. Yeh'kinya had led his helpers astray, and they were sent back to demand the egg from him.

Confronted, Yeh'kinya only gloated that it was too late. Hakkar was reborn in the ancient troll city of Zul'Gurub and grew in power there, and the troll thanked his dupes for hastening the Soulflayer's return.

Ironboot's worst fears had come. Legend spoke of the Soulflayer ruling the ancient troll world through terror, and he feared the new reign could spread across Azeroth. He sent the troll's former helpers to Molthor of the Zandalari on Yojamba Isle, off the coast of Stranglethorn, whose trolls might know how to defeat the blood god.

title: The Arcanite Buoy
body: When a hero brought Narain Soothfancy a ledger from the blue dragon Azuregos, the gnome learned that the dragon wanted an arcanite buoy built, and that its plans were written in Draconic, a tongue Narain cannot read. That old goat knows it, he grumbled. Before he could begin he needed three things, not necessarily in that order: his scrying goggles, a five hundred pound chicken, and volume two of Draconic for Dummies. For the chicken he sent his helper to Dirge Quikcleave, the cook of Gadgetzan. The book, he said, was stowed where no one could ever find it, on an island south of Land's End Beach.
sources: feralas.json note: Isle of Dread chimaerok chains left to Tanaris/Silithus
QuestHandler.cpp: autocomplete quests go straight to the reward window, no AddQuest
notes: Check: part 4 kept on DONE 8728: Narain offers 8729 at once (RewardNextQuest), so its warning of Maws in the Bay of Storms is read at that turn-in; it is the setup only, and the maelstrom, Maws and the shard stay with Silithus (DONE 8729). Part 1 reworded slightly. Converted: The three errands' outcomes moved out of the opening: Stewvul and the Molten Core to part 1 (QUEST_ACCEPT 8578, the crate quest), the chimaerok chops to part 2 (QUEST_DONE 8586), the booknapping and Weavil to part 3 (QUEST_ACCEPT 8620), the finished buoy and Maws to part 4 (QUEST_DONE 8728). 8729 stays Silithus's, so the Maws warning, from its description, is tied to the 8728 turn-in that offers it. Chain starts (8576) and ends (8728) with Narain in Tanaris; 8584 to 8587 run through Dirge in Gadgetzan; no Feralas trigger reused (feralas.json only names Lakmaeran in its Isle of Dread place). 8729 and the scepter left to Silithus. Text verified against 8575 to 8729. Faction 0: all AllowableRaces 0.

parts.body: The goggles had been stolen long ago by Stewvul, once Narain's best friend forever, who turned up hiding in a crate beside the Greymane Wall in Silverpine. He was glad to give them back, except that he had lost them a month before while nosing around in the Molten Core.
sources: DB: crate 180642 at the Greymane Wall (area 230)

parts.body: Dirge swore there was no such thing as a five hundred pound chicken, not anymore. Instead he had the carcass of the chimaerok lord, Lord Lakmaeran of the Isle of Dread in Feralas, brought to him, and with rocket fuel, deeprock salt and his own spices he made his greatest creation, Dirge's Kickin' Chimaerok Chops.

The book had been booknapped, a ransom note left in its place. A decoy drop in Winterspring failed, and the culprit proved to be Narain's arch-enemy, Doctor Weavil, who tore the only known copy into eight parts and scattered them to the wind. They had to be found and bound back together.

At last Narain read the ledger and, given a great deal of arcanite, elementium ore and rare gems, built the buoy. Only then did he mention the bad news: Maws, a hundred feet of death and destruction, waits where the buoy is meant to be cast, in the Bay of Storms off Azshara.

title: The Keepers of Time
body: In the mountains of eastern Tanaris, the threshold of the Caverns of Time is kept by the Steward of Time, one of the Keepers of Time who serve Nozdormu. He meets each traveler as though the visit had long been foreseen, and he does not hide the danger: beyond his hall, he warns, lie perils unheard of in the mortal world. For those willing to go on he offers a swift descent, one of his brothers flying them down to the master's lair far below, where Andormu of the Keepers of Time awaits the heroes the keepers have been expecting.
notes: Check: the opening no longer retells Andormu and Nozari's talk (creature_text 19932, 19933), spoken by that pair at another spot below and not heard at the 10279 accept; it now holds only what the Steward says and does (npc_text 9977, 9978, quest 10279), and the talk stays in 44029. Under mod-individual-progression the Steward stands behind the Caverns door (go_cavernsoftimedoor, gameobject 176996, seen only before state 8), so requiredState 8 follows the module as well. The custodian's tour moved out of the opening into parts on QUEST_ACCEPT 10277 (the keepers and the master's absence) and QUEST_DONE 10277 (the timeways and the Infinite Dragonflight). The opening keeps the Steward (10279, npc_text 9977, 9978) and Andormu and Nozari's talk (creature_text 19932, 19933). The tour's Stratholme line (broadcast 17669, patch 3.0) and Hyjal line not used. parts.body: Andormu sent a custodian to guide newcomers through the cavern. The keepers, she explained, watch over Nozdormu's realm and mend its ordinary disturbances, such as a rogue mage changing the past to raise his station. The master never meddles in mortal affairs and only corrects what others alter, yet he is away now, which means someone is trying to change time on a grand scale.

The tunnels around them are timeways, infinite in number. Those open now are trouble spots born of a single disturbance, ranked from least to most catastrophic, though the collapse of any one would end the world. At one she named the culprits, a malevolent organization called the Infinite Dragonflight. There are only two truths here, she said: time is always in flux, and perception does not dictate reality.
